summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 (general access) and Claude Mythos 5 (restricted, safeguards-lifted) as its next Mythos-class models with new safety classifiers, a 30-day data retention policy, and pricing of $10/$50 per million input/output tokens, before briefly suspending access days later and redeploying the models roughly three weeks after launch.

mechanisms.reason: The lab states this is its most capable generally-available model, state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5’s capabilities exceed those of any model we’ve ever made generally available. It is state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks of AI capability, showing exceptional performance in software engineering, knowledge work, vision, scientific research, and many other areas.

mechanisms.reason: The models are explicitly stated to work autonomously for longer horizons than any prior Claude model.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 can work autonomously for longer than any previous Claude models.

mechanisms.reason: The model is stated to maintain focus and use persistent notes across millions of tokens, increasing memory/context demands.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5 stays focused across millions of tokens in long-running tasks and improves its outputs using its own notes.

mechanisms.reason: The document states both very high expected demand for the new model and a subsequent suspension of access to it, pulling volume in both directions.
mechanisms.quote: We are suspending access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5.

mechanisms.reason: A customer testimonial reports the model achieving comparable results using a fraction of the reasoning tokens of a competitor, implying lower compute per unit of output.
mechanisms.quote: Claude Fable 5 is the strongest model we've tested on frontier physics research while using a third of the reasoning tokens.

categories.reason: The model is described accelerating drug design and gene-therapy research workflows by an order of magnitude, crossing into clinical/therapeutic development.
categories.quote: Using Mythos 5, our internal protein design experts accelerated aspects of the drug design process by around 10 times.

practices.reason: Concrete, stated gains in coding, analytical reasoning, and vision benchmarks give engineering teams evidence to upgrade production usage for these workloads.
practices.quote: During early testing, Stripe reported that Fable 5 compressed months of engineering into days. In a 50-million-line Ruby codebase, the model performed a codebase-wide migration in a day that would otherwise have taken a whole team over two months by hand.

practices.reason: The lab describes its own automated alignment assessment methodology and system-card safety evaluations, informative but not directly transferable to external teams.
practices.quote: In our automated alignment assessment, we found that Mythos 5’s level of misaligned behavior (including misaligned actions taken by the model such as deception and cooperation with misuse of the model by a user) was low, and similar to that of Opus 4.8.

practices.reason: A new mandatory 30-day data retention policy for Mythos-class model traffic requires teams to update data-handling and compliance processes.
practices.quote: We will require 30-day retention for all traffic on Mythos-class models, on both first- and third-party surfaces.

practices.reason: Persistent file-based memory is described as a technique that materially improved multi-step task performance, worth investigating for our own agent memory design.
practices.quote: When we had the model play the deck-building game Slay the Spire , giving it access to persistent file-based memory improved its performance three times more than for Opus 4.8; Fable also reached the game’s final act three times more often.

notable_reason: A frontier Anthropic model launch that was abruptly suspended days later and only redeployed weeks after is an unusual, high-visibility event for anyone tracking model releases and reliability.
